doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Writing charts: The Preacher for Benny Goodman
summary: Tommy's first Tonight Show charts, and an arrangement of The Preacher for Goodman that he was never paid for.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: When you would write a chart for the Tonight Show, how did that come about? Were you asked to write a chart? Did you say, “I want to write a chart” and then talk to the powers that be? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

It started, I submitted a couple. I wrote a couple of things, just ‘cause I wanted to do it. And I wanted to see if they would hire me doing that. And they liked them enough to play them and sometimes you get in some interesting, I got in an interesting bind between a band leader and Benny. And both of them thought the other one should pay.
Oh yeah? I don’t know this story.
It was an arrangement of “The Preacher.” Do you remember that a long time ago?
Yeah. There was one with clarinet that was for Benny for that show.
Yeah. Said Benny was to pay and Benny said he was. So I just ate that one.
And you know Benny Goodman’s not going to pay.
Yeah I was going to say, he wasn’t going to lose on that deal, right?
So that ended up being one of those things that about forty-five people Xeroxed and I never, just never got paid.
